title: Why Your Phone Dies in the Cold

sections.name: Why your phone dies in the cold
lines: You know when your phone dies in the cold,
even though it still had plenty of battery left?
Well, your battery isn't actually empty.
You see, it makes power by moving tiny particles called lithium ions
through a liquid inside the battery.
But when it gets cold, that liquid gets thick, almost like syrup.
So the ions can't move fast enough,
and your phone thinks the battery is dead, and shuts itself off.
But once it warms back up,
and most of that charge comes right back.
